sections.html:
Decatur, on the Tennessee River, anchors this county. Census takers found 123,421 residents in 2020, and the 2025 estimate has climbed to 126,483. Across 53,265 housing units there were 49,241 households. Vacancy ran 7.6%. Owners lived in 70.1% of occupied homes and tenants in the remaining 29.9%.

Country living is common. About 38.4% of residents are outside urban areas, so many sellers own a house on a larger lot or down a county road. Towns include Eva, Falkville, Priceville, Somerville and Trinity, alongside Decatur and Hartselle. A house's position relative to city limits determines which police, fire, utility and school services come with it, so say plainly where yours falls.

Three public systems divide the county: Decatur City Schools, Hartselle City Schools and Morgan County Schools. The property address controls the assignment, never the postal city. Check the district map, and if your lot hugs a boundary, state the district in any listing or in your note to a cash buyer.

The calendar is set statewide, and Morgan County follows it without local changes. The bill is payable beginning October 1. Once December 31 passes without payment, the account is delinquent. A parcel that nobody pays moves along like this:

MonthStep for an unpaid parcel
October 1Payment due
January 1Account turns late
FebruaryParcel passed to the probate court
MarchProbate court holds its session
AprilSale notice published
MayTax sale

Local offices at the Decatur courthouse keep the assessment, collection and probate files. Before listing, call the county and ask what your parcel owes today. Get it in writing, since buyers and title companies will ask.

Alabama exempts part of the assessed value on a single-family house if you own it, live in it and it was your primary residence on January 1 of the tax year. The limit is 160 acres. File at the county office.

  • Under 65 and not disabled: up to $4,000 of assessed value on the state portion.
  • Age 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled, or blind: no maximum on the state portion.
  • County exemptions: $2,000 of assessed value for most owners, with higher limits and income tests for seniors and disabled owners.

It is the owner who holds this benefit, never the house. Whoever buys yours starts without it until they file, which is why a purchaser's first bill can come in above what you paid. Expect a question about that from a buyer who is comparing bills.

sections.h2: Deed tax when a Morgan County house sells
sections.html:
The state levies a recordation tax of 50 cents on each $500 of value conveyed by a deed. Recording takes place at the probate judge's office, where staff want proof of the actual price. Two thirds of the revenue goes to the state treasury and one third to the county. Where a mortgage has already paid its own tax, that amount can come off the taxable value.

Deliberately withholding proof of value once asked invites a penalty of $100 or 25% of the tax due, whichever is greater. In most sales the closing agent collects the tax, and you see it as a single line on the settlement statement instead of making a separate courthouse trip.

Listing and cash sales share the same backbone of paperwork. Walking through it early avoids panic in the final week.

  1. Obtain the tax payoff figure and a mortgage payoff letter if a loan exists.
  2. Find the recorded deed and check each owner's name against the spelling on it.
  3. When an owner has died, settle who may sign before you accept any offer.
  4. Choose a closing agent, who runs the title search and builds the settlement statement.
  5. Liens and any open tax come out of proceeds, and the deed is then recorded with the probate judge.

Heirs living in another town often manage this by mail and phone. Mention that to the closing agent at the start, since arranging signatures from far away adds days.

Delinquent taxes can be paid off at the closing table, so the real problem is timing. Once a parcel is advertised in April, little time is left before the May sale. An owner near that point should ask the county office what stopping the process would take, then instruct the title company to pay the balance from proceeds.

People behind on taxes who want to dodge the spring sale sometimes choose a cash buyer, because a direct purchase can close sooner than a listing. The buyer still insists on a clean title, so the back taxes are paid during closing, never ignored.

A house passed to heirs is one of the most common reasons an owner here decides to sell. The heirs often live in another town and have no wish to keep paying for a place they will not occupy. Start with three questions. Who legally owns the house now? Who has authority to sign? Is a tax bill outstanding? Until those answers are clear, no buyer can close, whether the money comes from a bank or from cash.

A few habits save time. Keep the death records and any estate papers together in one folder. Photograph each room so a buyer who never visits can still judge the condition. Send the utility account details to the closing agent so final readings are handled cleanly. And confirm the tax mailing address, since notices sent to a deceased owner can sit unopened while the deadline approaches.

sections.h2: What Morgan County sellers run into
sections.html:
A lot of local sellers own an aging house, an inherited property or a rental that has stopped paying for itself. An as-is cash closing helps when the repairs needed to list a house would cost more than the owner can afford.

  • Decatur and Hartselle houses with deferred repairs.
  • Inherited property in Falkville, Somerville or Priceville.
  • Rural parcels with a house, outside city services.
  • Owners who are behind and want to get ahead of the tax sale.

Cash Home Buyers reviews Morgan County houses as they stand and sends a written offer. When the figure falls short, you owe nothing and can walk. A cash route bypasses the lender's appraisal, the repair demands after an inspection and the weeks of showings, so it attracts owners who cannot wait.

Before requesting an offer, gather the deed, your latest tax bill and a short list of known problems. Ask the buyer how quickly closing could happen and who pays for the title work, and get both answers on paper.

faqs.q: When are Morgan County, AL property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment is due October 1 and late after December 31. A parcel still unpaid reaches probate court in February, gets advertised in April and can be sold in May.

faqs.q: What is the deed tax in Morgan County, Alabama?
faqs.a: Fifty cents per $500 of the deed's value, under Alabama Code 40-22-1. It is paid at the probate judge's office as the deed is filed.

faqs.q: Can I get a homestead exemption in Morgan County?
faqs.a: Yes, when you live in the house as your main home on January 1 of the tax year. File at the county office. An owner under 65 can shield up to $4,000 of assessed value from state tax.

faqs.q: Which school district covers my Morgan County house?
faqs.a: The property address decides, not the mailing city. Decatur City Schools, Hartselle City Schools and Morgan County Schools each serve different areas.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Morgan County house that is behind on taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the county office for the payoff and tell the title company to deduct it from your proceeds. You have the most room if you move before the April advertisement.
